I5.quote: Hydrogen spillover (H-spillover) is the surface migration of activated hydrogen atoms from a metallic particle, on which they are generated, onto a support.

notes: Experimental plus DFT paper on H-spillover on Pd-doped oxidized CNTs; not computation only, not electrochemical, not a review, not retracted (record.json is_retracted false, no retraction statement in the text), no statement that its data were published before. I1 fails because no H2 uptake from the gas phase is measured by a gravimetric, volumetric or flow method. Evidence: main, p. 7, Section 2.1: 'Temperature-programmed desorption (TPD) measurements were carried out using the 3Flex (Micromeritics) combined with a mass spectrometer'; H2 TPD profiles are shown normalized in arbitrary units (main, p. 12, Figure 2c), with no uptake value. Spillover extent is read by WO3 reduction with UV-Vis DRS, normalized to 100% for Pd/CNT and 0% for Pd/CNT1000 (main, p. 14, Table 1, '%spillover'); this is not an H2 uptake quantity. N2 adsorption at -196 C gives surface area (220 and 232 m2 g-1, main, pp. 9-10) but is not H2 uptake. NAP-XPS used 1 mbar H2. Only main.txt was provided (no supplementary file); the Supporting Information list (main, p. 31) names TPD, XPS, STEM, UV-Vis and DFT items and no H2 uptake isotherms. Code chosen per the I1 rule: the paper has no H2 uptake value, so no_conditions_stated.
